Metrics in this section come from IBM Verify, which records two different kinds
of event. It raises an **authentication event** when someone presents an
authentication method to CanadaLogin: a password, then a second factor. It raises
an **SSO event** when someone who is already signed in reaches a partner service,
and files that one under *application usage*. These are separate
event types, so a figure taken from one is never comparable to a figure taken
from the other.

A user signs in to CanadaLogin once and gets a session. Reaching a partner
service afterwards does not sign them in again: CanadaLogin uses the session it
already holds and issues the partner a freshly minted assertion or token. One
sign-in, then as many handoffs as the user needs.

| Term | Means | Which table |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in | The human act: a password, then a second factor | None counts it directly |
| Authentication event | What IBM Verify records while that happens. Runs ahead of sign-ins | `auth_total_logins` |
| Session | The signed-in state at CanadaLogin, reusable by later handoffs | None |
| SSO event | The session being used to reach a partner service | `app_login_counts` |

"Sign-in" is prose only. No table counts it, so it is never an output column
name or an axis label, and names a metric only where that metric is labelled an
estimate.

The relevant IBM Verify tables are:

- [`ibm_verify.auth_total_logins`](../catalog/ibm_verify/auth_total_logins.qmd) - daily, CanadaLogin-wide authentication-event totals
- [`ibm_verify.app_login_counts`](../catalog/ibm_verify/app_login_counts.qmd) - daily SSO event counts broken down by application
- [`ibm_verify.mfa_activity`](../catalog/ibm_verify/mfa_activity.qmd) - multi-factor authentication activity by factor and result

**Internal applications.** Internal applications are typically excluded from
public-facing adoption metrics. Which ones are internal comes from
[`rp.service.is_internal`](../catalog/rp/service.qmd), resolved to IBM Verify's
application names through [`rp.alias`](../catalog/rp/alias.qmd):

```sql
SELECT al.alias
FROM   rp.alias al
JOIN   rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
WHERE  s.is_internal
```

Use the subquery rather than a pasted list, so the classification stays in one
place. See the internal applications note in [notes.qmd](notes.qmd).

## CanadaLogin Metrics

Metrics in this section describe CanadaLogin overall, across all applications,
sourced mainly from `ibm_verify.auth_total_logins` (the estimated sessions metric
also draws on `ibm_verify.mfa_activity`).

::: {#metrics-1}
:::

## Application Metrics

Metrics in this section describe how much each application is used, sourced from
`ibm_verify.app_login_counts`. IBM Verify records this as SSO events, filed under
*application usage*: someone who is already signed in reaching a service. The
person enters no password and no second factor, which is why these counts are not
inflated the way the CanadaLogin-wide authentication events are.

::: {#metrics-2}
:::

## Multi-factor Authentication Metrics

Metrics in this section describe multi-factor authentication (MFA) activity,
sourced from `ibm_verify.mfa_activity`. That table has one row per day per MFA
factor (`mfa_type`) per outcome (`result`), with the number of attempts in
`count`.

IBM Verify files MFA as a subtype of the authentication event rather than as an
event type of its own, so these counts are a slice of the CanadaLogin-wide
authentication events, not a separate stream.

::: {#metrics-3}
:::
